notes.text:
This card demonstrates its own edge case: it counts **three** `kb:` blocks — one real, plus two the
"What" section quotes as examples inside backticks. So the doctor check in item 4 must not be a
naive count.

What separates a real block from a quoted one is the same thing `parseBodyBlock` already relies on:
position. A machine block is at the very top of the body; anything else is prose, whether or not it
is fenced. So the check is "more than one block that starts at column 0 of its own line, outside a
code fence" — and even that flags a card whose prose legitimately opens a line with the syntax.

Cheaper and exact: flag a card only when a second block would change the card if it were the first
— i.e. it parses as JSON and its keys differ from the governing block. A quoted `<!-- kb: … -->`
with an ellipsis does not parse, so it never fires. That also makes the message actionable: name
the keys that disagree, which is the drift the card is actually about.
